# Tools

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:tools`. Do not edit by hand. -->

200 tools across 9 toolsets: 80 read, 67 write, 53 destroy.
Plus 3 setup tools that are always available.

The **Access** column is the permission tier a tool needs:

- `read` — always available.
- `write` — creates or modifies data. Needs `--allow-write` (or `MONEYBIRD_ALLOW_WRITE=true`).
- `destroy` — deletes data, or does something the API offers no way to undo. Needs both
  `--allow-write` and `--allow-delete`.

Tools outside those tiers are not registered at all, so a model cannot see or call them.
Run `moneybird-mcp tools` to list what your current settings expose.

Toolsets enabled by default: core, invoicing, purchases, banking, time.

## Setup

Always registered, whatever the toolset and permission settings, because they are how a server
with no working credentials gets some.

| Tool | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connect_moneybird` | read | Authenticate this server against a Moneybird account. Call it when other tools report missing or rejected credentials. It opens the Moneybird token page and stores the token you create. |
| `moneybird_connection_status` | read | Report whether this server has working Moneybird credentials, which administration is selected, and which administrations the token can reach. |
| `select_administration` | read | Change the administration that tools use when they are not given an explicit administration_id. Applies for the rest of this session. |

## core

Administrations, contacts, products, ledger accounts, tax rates, identities and users.

_Enabled by default._

| Tool | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_administrations` | read | List every Moneybird administration this token can access, with id, name, language, currency and country. Use this first to discover the administration id other tools need. |
| `list_contacts` | read | List or search contacts (customers and suppliers). Supply `query` for free-text search across name, email, phone, customer id, tax number and address, or `filter` for structured narrowing. |
| `get_contact` | read | Retrieve a single contact by its Moneybird id, or by your own `customer_id` reference. |
| `create_contact` | write | Create a contact. Supply `company_name` for a company, or `firstname` and `lastname` for a person. |
| `update_contact` | write | Update a contact. Only the attributes you supply are changed. |
| `archive_contact` | write | Archive a contact, hiding it from pickers while keeping its history. Prefer this over deleting. |
| `delete_contact` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently delete a contact. Moneybird refuses this when the contact still has documents attached; archive it instead in that case. |
| `create_contact_person` | write | Add a contact person to an existing contact. |
| `update_contact_person` | write | Update a contact person belonging to a contact. |
| `delete_contact_person` | destroy (irreversible) | Remove a contact person from a contact. |
| `add_contact_note` | write | Attach a note to a contact. Notes can optionally be flagged as a to-do with an assignee. |
| `list_products` | read | List the product catalogue, optionally narrowed by free-text query or currency. |
| `get_product` | read | Retrieve a product by Moneybird id or by its `identifier`. |
| `create_product` | write | Add a product to the catalogue. |
| `update_product` | write | Update a product in the catalogue. |
| `delete_product` | destroy (irreversible) | Delete a product from the catalogue. |
| `list_tax_rates` | read | List the VAT rates configured for the administration. Invoice lines reference these by `tax_rate_id`. |
| `list_ledger_accounts` | read | List the chart of accounts. Bookings and invoice lines reference these by `ledger_account_id`. |
| `get_ledger_account` | read | Retrieve a single ledger account. |
| `create_ledger_account` | write | Add an account to the chart of accounts. |
| `update_ledger_account` | write | Update an account in the chart of accounts. |
| `delete_ledger_account` | destroy (irreversible) | Delete an account from the chart of accounts. |
| `list_identities` | read | List the identities (sender profiles) an administration can invoice under, including the default one. |
| `get_identity` | read | Retrieve one identity, or the administration default when no id is given. |
| `create_identity` | write | Create a new sender identity for the administration. |
| `update_identity` | write | Update a sender identity, or the default one when no id is given. |
| `delete_identity` | destroy (irreversible) | Delete a sender identity. |
| `list_custom_fields` | read | List the custom fields defined for contacts, sales invoices and identities, with the ids needed to set them. |
| `list_document_styles` | read | List the document styles (invoice and estimate layouts) of the administration. |
| `list_users` | read | List the users with access to the administration, with their ids and permissions. |

## invoicing

Sales invoices, recurring invoices, estimates, external sales invoices and subscriptions.

_Enabled by default._

| Tool | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_sales_invoices` | read | List sales invoices. Defaults to the current financial year, so pass an explicit `period` in the filter to look further back. |
| `get_sales_invoice` | read | Retrieve one sales invoice by its Moneybird id, including its lines, payments and notes. |
| `find_sales_invoice_by_invoice_id` | read | Look up a sales invoice by its printed invoice number, e.g. "2025-0001". Drafts have no invoice number and are never found this way. |
| `find_sales_invoice_by_reference` | read | Look up a sales invoice by the `reference` you set on it, e.g. a PO or project code. |
| `create_sales_invoice` | write | Create a sales invoice as a draft. Supply `contact_id` and the lines in `details_attributes`; send it afterwards with send_sales_invoice. |
| `update_sales_invoice` | write | Update a sales invoice. Only the attributes you supply change. Supplying `details_attributes` without the `id` of an existing line adds a line rather than replacing the set. |
| `delete_sales_invoice` | destroy (irreversible) | Delete a sales invoice. Moneybird refuses this when the invoice has payments or falls in a locked bookkeeping period. |
| `send_sales_invoice` | destroy (irreversible) | Send a sales invoice to the customer, or schedule it for a future date. With no arguments the contact and workflow defaults are used. This reaches the customer and cannot be recalled. |
| `register_sales_invoice_payment` | destroy (irreversible) | Record a payment against a sales invoice, marking it (partly) paid. This books a mutation; correcting it means deleting the payment again. |
| `mark_sales_invoice_as_dubious` | write | Flag a sales invoice as doubtful debt. Bookkeeping only; it does not write the invoice off. |
| `mark_sales_invoice_as_uncollectible` | destroy (irreversible) | Write a sales invoice off as uncollectible. This books a correction in the ledger and closes the invoice. |
| `download_sales_invoice_pdf` | read | Return a download URL for the invoice PDF. The link is signed and expires after 30 seconds, so use it immediately. |
| `add_sales_invoice_note` | write | Attach an internal note to a sales invoice. Notes are never shown to the customer and can be flagged as a to-do with an assignee. |
| `list_estimates` | read | List estimates (quotes). Defaults to the current financial year, so pass an explicit `period` in the filter to look further back. |
| `get_estimate` | read | Retrieve one estimate by its Moneybird id, or by the estimate number printed on the document (`estimate_number`, e.g. "2025-0001"). |
| `create_estimate` | write | Create an estimate (quote) as a draft. Supply `contact_id` and the lines in `details_attributes`; send it afterwards with send_estimate. |
| `update_estimate` | write | Update an estimate. Only the attributes you supply change. |
| `delete_estimate` | destroy (irreversible) | Delete an estimate. |
| `send_estimate` | destroy (irreversible) | Send an estimate to the customer. With no arguments the contact and workflow defaults are used. This reaches the customer and cannot be recalled. |
| `bill_estimate` | destroy (irreversible) | Turn an accepted or open estimate into a sales invoice. The invoice is created as a draft; send it separately with send_sales_invoice. |
| `download_estimate_pdf` | read | Return a download URL for the estimate PDF. The link is signed and expires after 30 seconds, so use it immediately. |
| `list_recurring_sales_invoices` | read | List the recurring invoice schedules. Only active schedules are returned unless the filter says otherwise. |
| `get_recurring_sales_invoice` | read | Retrieve one recurring invoice schedule, including its lines and next invoice date. |
| `create_recurring_sales_invoice` | write | Create a schedule that generates sales invoices automatically. Needs `contact_id`, `details_attributes` and a planning: `invoice_date` for the first invoice plus `frequency` and `frequency_type`. |
| `update_recurring_sales_invoice` | write | Update a recurring invoice schedule. Moneybird refuses this while an active subscription drives the schedule. |
| `delete_recurring_sales_invoice` | destroy (irreversible) | Stop a recurring invoice schedule. It is deleted when it never produced an invoice, and deactivated otherwise so the invoices it created stay intact. |
| `list_external_sales_invoices` | read | List revenue invoiced outside Moneybird, e.g. by a webshop or POS. Defaults to the current financial year, so pass an explicit `period` in the filter to look further back. |
| `get_external_sales_invoice` | read | Retrieve one external sales invoice, including its lines and payments. |
| `create_external_sales_invoice` | write | Book revenue that was invoiced outside Moneybird. Unlike a sales invoice this is never sent to the customer; it only records the amounts and their ledger accounts. |
| `update_external_sales_invoice` | write | Update an external sales invoice. Only the attributes you supply change. |
| `delete_external_sales_invoice` | destroy (irreversible) | Delete an external sales invoice and the revenue it booked. |
| `register_external_sales_invoice_payment` | destroy (irreversible) | Record a payment against an external sales invoice, marking it (partly) paid. This books a mutation. |
| `list_subscriptions` | read | List the subscriptions of one contact. Moneybird has no administration-wide subscription list, so `contact_id` is required. |
| `get_subscription` | read | Retrieve one subscription, including its product, billing cycle and recurring invoice. |
| `create_subscription` | write | Subscribe a contact to a product. Moneybird creates the recurring sales invoice behind it and bills from `start_date`, at the earliest tomorrow. |
| `update_subscription` | write | Change the product, quantity or settings of a subscription. Switching product makes Moneybird bill the price difference for the remaining period on a one-off invoice. |
| `cancel_subscription` | destroy (irreversible) | Cancel a subscription and stop its recurring invoices. Pass `end_date` to let it run until a future date. |
| `list_subscription_templates` | read | List the subscription templates of the administration. Requires the `settings` scope rather than `sales_invoices`. |
| `delete_sales_invoice_payment` | destroy (irreversible) | Remove a payment from a sales invoice, returning the invoice to unpaid for that amount. Payment ids come from the invoice itself via get_sales_invoice. |
| `delete_external_sales_invoice_payment` | destroy (irreversible) | Remove a payment from an external sales invoice. Payment ids come from get_external_sales_invoice. |

## purchases

Purchase invoices, receipts, documents and general journal documents.

_Enabled by default._

| Tool | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_purchase_invoices` | read | List purchase invoices (bills received from suppliers), newest first. Narrow with `filter`; keys: period (named period such as this_year/prev_quarter, or a range like 20260101..20260131), state (all\|new\|saved\|open\|paid\|late\|pending_payment — paid, late and pending_payment only apply to purchase invoices and receipts), recurring (all\|enabled\|disabled), attachment (all\|with\|without), reference, contact_id, ledger_account_id, updated_after (ISO 8601 UTC). |
| `get_purchase_invoice` | read | Retrieve one purchase invoice by id, with its lines, payments, attachments and notes. |
| `create_purchase_invoice` | write | Book a supplier invoice. Supply `contact_id` for the supplier, the supplier `reference` and `date`, and one line per amount in `details_attributes`. |
| `update_purchase_invoice` | write | Update a purchase invoice. Only the attributes you supply change; to edit a line pass its `id` inside `details_attributes`, and to drop one pass its `id` with `_destroy: true`. |
| `delete_purchase_invoice` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently delete a purchase invoice, including its lines and bookings. |
| `register_purchase_invoice_payment` | destroy (irreversible) | Record a payment against a purchase invoice, marking it (partly) paid. Give `payment_date` and `price`, plus either `financial_mutation_id` to settle a bank mutation or a `manual_payment_action`. |
| `list_receipts` | read | List receipts (expenses paid on the spot, without a supplier invoice). Narrow with `filter`; keys: period (named period such as this_year/prev_quarter, or a range like 20260101..20260131), state (all\|new\|saved\|open\|paid\|late\|pending_payment — paid, late and pending_payment only apply to purchase invoices and receipts), recurring (all\|enabled\|disabled), attachment (all\|with\|without), reference, contact_id, ledger_account_id, updated_after (ISO 8601 UTC). |
| `get_receipt` | read | Retrieve one receipt by id, with its lines, payments, attachments and notes. |
| `create_receipt` | write | Book a receipt. Pass `financial_account_id` to record it as already paid from that account. |
| `update_receipt` | write | Update a receipt. Only the attributes you supply change; to edit a line pass its `id` inside `details_attributes`, and to drop one pass its `id` with `_destroy: true`. |
| `delete_receipt` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently delete a receipt, including its lines and bookings. |
| `register_receipt_payment` | destroy (irreversible) | Record a payment against a receipt, marking it (partly) paid. Give `payment_date` and `price`, plus either `financial_mutation_id` to settle a bank mutation or a `manual_payment_action`. |
| `list_general_documents` | read | List general documents: filed paperwork such as contracts and correspondence that carries a date and reference but no amounts. Narrow with `filter`; keys: period (named period such as this_year/prev_quarter, or a range like 20260101..20260131), state (all\|new\|saved\|open\|paid\|late\|pending_payment — paid, late and pending_payment only apply to purchase invoices and receipts), recurring (all\|enabled\|disabled), attachment (all\|with\|without), reference, contact_id, ledger_account_id, updated_after (ISO 8601 UTC). |
| `get_general_document` | read | Retrieve one general document by id, with its attachments and notes. |
| `create_general_document` | write | File a general document. `reference` and `date` are required. |
| `update_general_document` | write | Update a general document. Set `remove_contact` to detach the contact currently linked to it. |
| `delete_general_document` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently delete a general document and its attachments. |
| `list_general_journal_documents` | read | List general journal documents (manual journal entries). Narrow with `filter`; keys: period (named period such as this_year/prev_quarter, or a range like 20260101..20260131), state (all\|new\|saved\|open\|paid\|late\|pending_payment — paid, late and pending_payment only apply to purchase invoices and receipts), recurring (all\|enabled\|disabled), attachment (all\|with\|without), reference, contact_id, ledger_account_id, updated_after (ISO 8601 UTC). |
| `get_general_journal_document` | read | Retrieve one general journal document by id, with its debit and credit entries. |
| `create_general_journal_document` | write | Book a manual journal entry. `general_journal_document_entries_attributes` takes either a list of entries or an object keyed by index — the two forms are interchangeable, so pick one and do not mix them. Each entry names a `ledger_account_id` and carries either `debit` or `credit`, never both, and the debit total must equal the credit total. |
| `update_general_journal_document` | write | Update a manual journal entry. Entries you pass in `general_journal_document_entries_attributes` need their `id` to be changed or `_destroy: true` to be removed; entries you leave out stay as they are, and the debit and credit totals must still match afterwards. |
| `delete_general_journal_document` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently delete a manual journal entry and reverse its bookings. |
| `list_typeless_documents` | read | List typeless documents: uploads parked in Moneybird that have not been classified as an invoice, receipt or anything else yet. Narrow with `filter`; keys: period (named period such as this_year/prev_quarter, or a range like 20260101..20260131), state (all\|new\|saved\|open\|paid\|late\|pending_payment — paid, late and pending_payment only apply to purchase invoices and receipts), recurring (all\|enabled\|disabled), attachment (all\|with\|without), reference, contact_id, ledger_account_id, updated_after (ISO 8601 UTC). |
| `get_typeless_document` | read | Retrieve one typeless document by id, with its attachments. |
| `create_typeless_document` | write | Create a typeless document to park an upload that has not been classified yet. Moneybird offers no update endpoint for this type, so its reference, date and contact are fixed at creation — only its attachments can be changed afterwards. Delete and recreate it to correct a mistake. |
| `delete_typeless_document` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently delete a typeless document and its attachments. |
| `add_document_note` | write | Attach a note to a purchase invoice, receipt, general document or general journal document. A note can be flagged as a to-do and assigned to a user. |
| `download_document_attachment` | read | Return a temporary download URL for one attachment of a document. Get the attachment ids from the document itself with get_purchase_invoice, get_receipt or the matching get tool. |
| `delete_document_attachment` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently remove one attachment from a document; the document itself is kept. |
| `delete_document_payment` | destroy (irreversible) | Remove a payment from a purchase invoice or receipt, putting the document back to unpaid for that amount. |

## banking

Financial accounts, financial mutations, payments and purchase transactions.

_Enabled by default._

| Tool | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_financial_accounts` | read | List the bank and payment provider accounts of the administration, with the ids that financial mutations and statements reference as `financial_account_id`. |
| `list_financial_mutations` | read | List bank transactions. Without a filter Moneybird returns the current financial year only, so pass an explicit `period` to look further back. |
| `get_financial_mutation` | read | Retrieve one bank transaction by id, including the payments and ledger bookings currently linked to it. |
| `link_booking` | destroy (irreversible) | Book a bank transaction against a record: an invoice, a purchase transaction or a ledger account. This posts to the ledger. Omit `price` to book the full mutation amount. |
| `unlink_booking` | destroy (irreversible) | Remove a payment or ledger booking from a bank transaction, returning the mutation to unprocessed. Call get_financial_mutation first to read the `booking_id` off the existing link. |
| `get_payment` | read | Retrieve a payment by id, whichever document it belongs to. Payment ids appear on invoices, receipts and on the bookings of a financial mutation. |
| `list_purchase_transactions` | read | List outgoing payment instructions (purchase transactions). Moneybird defaults to `unbatched:true`, so pass an explicit filter to see transactions already collected into a batch. |
| `get_purchase_transaction` | read | Retrieve one purchase transaction by id, with its amount, state and the document it pays. |
| `delete_purchase_transaction` | destroy (irreversible) | Delete a purchase transaction, cancelling the payment instruction it represents. |

## time

Time entries and projects.

_Enabled by default._

| Tool | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_time_entries` | read | List tracked time. Without a filter Moneybird returns the current financial year, so pass an explicit `period` to look further back, and `include_active:true` to see timers that are still running. |
| `get_time_entry` | read | Retrieve a single time entry by id, with its contact, project, user and billable state. |
| `create_time_entry` | write | Log time for a user. `user_id`, `started_at` and `description` are required; call list_users for the id. Omitting `ended_at` starts a running timer. |
| `update_time_entry` | write | Update a time entry. Only the attributes you supply are changed. `user_id` cannot be changed after creation. |
| `stop_time_entry` | write | Stop a running timer, setting `ended_at` to now. |
| `resume_time_entry` | write | Restart a stopped time entry, clearing `ended_at` so the timer runs again. |
| `delete_time_entry` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently delete a time entry. |
| `add_time_entry_note` | write | Attach a note to a time entry, optionally flagged as a to-do with an assignee. |
| `delete_time_entry_note` | destroy (irreversible) | Remove a note from a time entry. |
| `list_projects` | read | List projects. Moneybird returns only active projects unless the filter says otherwise. Time entries reference these by `project_id`. |
| `get_project` | read | Retrieve a single project by id, with its name, state and budget. |
| `create_project` | write | Create a project to book time and costs against. The name must be unique in the administration. |
| `update_project` | write | Rename a project or change its budget. Moneybird requires `name` on every update. |
| `delete_project` | destroy (irreversible) | Delete a project. Moneybird refuses this while time entries are still booked on it. |

## reports

Profit and loss, balance sheet, the other `/reports` endpoints, financial statements and downloads.

_Off by default. Enable with `--toolsets core,invoicing,purchases,banking,time,reports` or `--toolsets all`._

| Tool | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_profit_loss_report` | read | Profit and loss over a period, broken down per ledger account. Nested ledger accounts are listed flat, so a parent amount excludes its children and the items of a section sum to that section without double counting. Sections are not signed alike: revenue and other income are credit minus debit, direct costs and expenses are debit minus credit. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_balance_sheet_report` | read | Balance sheet showing assets, liabilities and equity as they stand at the end of the period. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_general_ledger_report` | read | Every ledger account with its opening balance, movements and closing balance over the period. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_cash_flow_report` | read | Cash received and cash paid during the period, optionally for a single financial account. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_tax_report` | read | VAT return figures for the period: turnover and VAT per rate, plus input VAT to reclaim. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_assets_report` | read | Fixed asset overview for the period, with purchase value, depreciation and book value per asset. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_subscriptions_report` | read | Recurring revenue for the period, based on the administration's subscriptions. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_journal_entries_report` | read | Individual bookings in the period, narrowed by project, contact or ledger account. At least one of `project_id`, `contact_id` or `ledger_account_id` is required, and `account_type` additionally requires `contact_id` or `project_id`. This is the drill-down behind the revenue and expenses reports: pair `account_type: "revenue"` with a project or contact for revenue detail, and run `"expenses"` and `"direct_costs"` separately for expense detail. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_ledger_account_report` | read | Bookings on a single ledger account for the period. Deprecated by Moneybird in favour of get_journal_entries_report with `ledger_account_id`; prefer that tool for new work. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_revenue_by_contact_report` | read | Revenue in the period totalled per contact. Use get_journal_entries_report with the contact id for the underlying bookings. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_expenses_by_contact_report` | read | Expenses in the period totalled per contact (supplier). Use get_journal_entries_report with the contact id for the underlying bookings. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_revenue_by_project_report` | read | Revenue in the period totalled per project. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_expenses_by_project_report` | read | Expenses in the period totalled per project. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_debtors_report` | read | Outstanding customer balances at the end of the period. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_creditors_report` | read | Outstanding supplier balances at the end of the period. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_debtors_aging_report` | read | Outstanding customer balances bucketed by how long they have been overdue, up to `period_until`. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `get_creditors_aging_report` | read | Outstanding supplier balances bucketed by how long they have been overdue, up to `period_until`. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `export_auditfile` | write | Queue an XAF auditfile export for a calendar year. Returns nothing: the file is prepared asynchronously and shows up in list_downloads, from where get_download_url hands out the link. Fails when ledger accounts have missing or duplicate account ids, or when the year holds no journal entries. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `export_brugstaat` | write | Queue a brugstaat XML export for a calendar year. Returns nothing: the file is prepared asynchronously and shows up in list_downloads, from where get_download_url hands out the link. Requires every ledger account to carry a valid RGS taxonomy code. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `export_ledger_accounts` | write | Queue an Excel export of the ledger account cards (grootboekkaarten) with all bookings for a calendar year. Returns nothing: the file is prepared asynchronously and shows up in list_downloads, from where get_download_url hands out the link. Reports have their own tighter rate limit of 50 requests per 5 minutes (the rest of the API allows 150), so pick the one report that answers the question instead of calling several. |
| `list_downloads` | read | List the prepared export files of the administration, newest first, with their id, type and status. This is where the files queued by export_auditfile, export_brugstaat and export_ledger_accounts arrive. |
| `get_download_url` | read | Return the temporary URL of a prepared export file. Takes the download id from list_downloads; the URL is valid for 30 seconds, so fetch it right away. |
| `create_financial_statement` | write | Create a bank statement on a financial account and group transactions into it. Each transaction becomes a financial mutation that can then be reconciled against documents. |
| `update_financial_statement` | write | Update a bank statement. Only the attributes you supply change. Mutations carrying an `id` are updated, those without one are added, and `_destroy: true` removes one from the statement. |
| `delete_financial_statement` | destroy (irreversible) | Delete a bank statement together with the financial mutations it groups, removing those transactions from the administration. |

## assets

Fixed assets and their depreciation.

_Off by default. Enable with `--toolsets core,invoicing,purchases,banking,time,assets` or `--toolsets all`._

| Tool | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_assets` | read | List the fixed assets of the administration with their purchase value, depreciation plan and current book value. Only active assets are returned unless `active` is set to false. |
| `get_asset` | read | Retrieve one fixed asset with its value changes, sources and disposal. Also the way to check the result of create_asset_retroactive_value_changes, which runs asynchronously. |
| `create_asset` | write | Create a fixed asset. `name`, `ledger_account_id`, `purchase_date` and `purchase_value` are required. Supply `value_change_plan_attributes` for the depreciation plan; assets on a land or building ledger account never depreciate and must leave it out, every other ledger account requires it. |
| `update_asset` | write | Update a fixed asset. Once the asset is active — its purchase date has passed — Moneybird accepts a change to `name` only. |
| `delete_asset` | destroy (irreversible) | Delete a fixed asset together with its depreciation history. Moneybird refuses this once bookings depend on it. |
| `create_asset_manual_value_change` | destroy (irreversible) | Book a one-off depreciation or revaluation on an asset at a given date. A negative amount lowers the value, a positive amount raises it; an amount above the value at that date is rejected. This writes to the depreciation history and the booking cannot be undone through the API. |
| `create_asset_arbitrary_value_change` | destroy (irreversible) | Book a value change that breaks the depreciation schedule, for example an impairment. Every linear value change after this date is removed; call create_asset_retroactive_value_changes afterwards to rebuild the schedule. Irreversible through the API. |
| `create_asset_divestment` | destroy (irreversible) | Divest an asset at a date: its remaining value leaves the balance sheet and the profit is booked as book result. Moneybird sets the amount itself, creates a disposal and drops every linear value change after the date. Irreversible through the API. |
| `create_asset_full_depreciation` | destroy (irreversible) | Write an asset off completely at a date: its remaining value leaves the balance sheet without a book result. Moneybird sets the amount itself, creates a disposal and drops every linear value change after the date. Irreversible through the API. |
| `create_asset_retroactive_value_changes` | destroy (irreversible) | Fill in the linear depreciation entries an asset is still missing, from its purchase date or last arbitrary value change up to the last month of the administration. Needs an asset with a depreciation plan, remaining value and gaps outside the locked period. Runs asynchronously and returns nothing — poll get_asset for the result. |
| `create_asset_disposal` | destroy (irreversible) | Record that an asset left the administration on a date, with a reason. Requires the asset to be fully depreciated — its value at the disposal date must be zero — and to have no disposal yet. Irreversible through the API. |
| `add_asset_source` | write | Link the booking an asset was purchased with to that asset. Provide exactly one of `detail_id` (a line of a purchase invoice or receipt) or `general_journal_document_entry_id` — never both. The booking must sit on the same ledger account as the asset. |
| `delete_asset_source` | destroy (irreversible) | Unlink a source booking from an asset. The booking and the asset themselves stay; only the link is removed. |
| `create_asset_reinvestment_reserve_purchase` | write | Record that part of the asset's purchase value is funded from the reinvestment reserve (herinvesteringsreserve). The amount may not exceed the depreciatable value (purchase value minus residual value), and the purchase date may not lie in the locked period. |
| `delete_asset_reinvestment_reserve_purchase` | destroy (irreversible) | Remove the reinvestment reserve funding from an asset. |
| `create_asset_reinvestment_reserve_sale` | write | Book the book result of an asset's disposal to the reinvestment reserve (herinvesteringsreserve). Requires the asset to already have a disposal whose date lies outside the locked period. |
| `delete_asset_reinvestment_reserve_sale` | destroy (irreversible) | Remove the reinvestment reserve booking from an asset's disposal. |

## tasks

Task lists, tasks, task list templates and workflows.

_Off by default. Enable with `--toolsets core,invoicing,purchases,banking,time,tasks` or `--toolsets all`._

| Tool | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_task_lists` | read | List the task lists of an administration. Moneybird returns 30 per page; the response does not include the tasks themselves, so call get_task_list for the contents of one. |
| `get_task_list` | read | Retrieve one task list with its groups, tasks and subtasks. |
| `create_task_list` | write | Create a task list. `name` is required. Pass `template_id` to build it from a task list template, which is the same as calling create_task_list_from_template. |
| `update_task_list` | write | Update the name, description or deadline of a task list. |
| `delete_task_list` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently delete a task list together with all its groups and tasks. |
| `create_task_list_group` | write | Add a group to a task list. Groups hold the tasks; give a `report_type` to have Moneybird generate the group's tasks from that report instead of adding them by hand. |
| `get_task_list_group` | read | Retrieve one task list group with its tasks. |
| `update_task_list_group` | write | Rename a task list group or change its report type. Changing `report_type` destroys the existing tasks in the group and regenerates them from the new report. |
| `delete_task_list_group` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently delete a task list group and every task in it. |
| `create_task` | write | Add a task to a task list group. Needs the group id, not the task list id — get_task_list lists the groups with their ids. |
| `get_task` | read | Retrieve one task with its subtasks, notes and events. |
| `update_task` | write | Update a task. Only the attributes you supply are changed. |
| `delete_task` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently delete a task and its subtasks. Moneybird refuses this for generated tasks — delete or re-type their group instead. |
| `assign_task` | write | Assign a user to a task, or clear the assignment by omitting `assignee_id`. The user must already have access to the task; Moneybird answers 404 when they do not. list_users gives the user ids. |
| `complete_task` | write | Mark a task and all of its subtasks as completed. |
| `reopen_task` | write | Reopen a completed task, along with any parent tasks that were completed with it. |
| `add_task_note` | write | Attach a note to a task, optionally flagged as a to-do. |
| `list_task_list_templates` | read | List the task list templates of an administration. Templates are the blueprints that create_task_list_from_template instantiates. |
| `get_task_list_template` | read | Retrieve one task list template with its groups and tasks. |
| `create_task_list_template` | write | Create a task list template. `name` is required; `period` and `deadline_after` control the recurrence and deadline of the lists made from it. |
| `update_task_list_template` | write | Update a task list template. Existing task lists already created from it are not changed. |
| `delete_task_list_template` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently delete a task list template and all its groups and tasks. |
| `create_task_list_template_group` | write | Add a group to a task list template, so lists made from it start with that group. |
| `create_task_list_from_template` | write | Instantiate a task list template into a new task list, copying its groups and tasks. Every attribute is optional and falls back to the template. |
| `list_workflows` | read | List the invoice and estimate workflows of the administration, with their reminder steps. Contacts and documents reference these by `invoice_workflow_id` and `estimate_workflow_id`. |
| `get_workflow` | read | Retrieve one workflow, including its currency, language, payment methods and reminder steps. |

## webhooks

Webhook subscriptions, the customer contact portal and verifications.

_Off by default. Enable with `--toolsets core,invoicing,purchases,banking,time,webhooks` or `--toolsets all`._

| Tool | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_webhooks` | read | List the webhooks registered on the administration, with their url, subscribed events and the status code Moneybird last got back from each. There is no endpoint for a single webhook, so read one from this list. |
| `create_webhook` | destroy (irreversible) | Register a webhook: Moneybird will POST a payload to `url` whenever a subscribed event happens in this administration, so the endpoint receives contact, invoice and document data from then on. Use HTTPS — over plain HTTP that data travels in the clear. The url must answer 200 at creation. Leave `enabled_events` empty to receive everything, or name events: contact_created, contact_changed, sales_invoice_created, sales_invoice_updated, sales_invoice_send_email, sales_invoice_send_si, sales_invoice_paused, sales_invoice_unpaused, sales_invoice_marked_as_dubious, sales_invoice_marked_as_uncollectible, sales_invoice_state_changed_to_open, sales_invoice_state_changed_to_paid, sales_invoice_state_changed_to_scheduled, sales_invoice_state_changed_to_uncollectible, sales_invoice_created_based_on_estimate, credit_invoice_created_from_original, recurring_sales_invoice_created, estimate_created, estimate_updated, estimate_send_email, estimate_mark_accepted, external_sales_invoice_created, external_sales_invoice_updated, external_sales_invoice_marked_as_dubious, external_sales_invoice_marked_as_uncollectible, external_sales_invoice_state_changed_to_uncollectible, document_saved, document_updated, time_entry_created, time_entry_updated, task_lists_task_created, task_lists_task_assigned, task_lists_task_completed, task_lists_task_reopened, task_lists_task_name. The response carries a `secret` that is returned only once; it signs the payloads Moneybird sends. |
| `activate_webhook` | write | Reactivate a deactivated webhook so it receives event notifications again. |
| `deactivate_webhook` | write | Stop a webhook from receiving new events without removing it; retries already queued still run. Reversible with activate_webhook, which makes this the safer alternative to delete_webhook. |
| `delete_webhook` | destroy (irreversible) | Permanently remove a webhook registration. Re-creating it later yields a new token and secret, so deactivate_webhook is the better choice for a temporary pause. |
| `create_customer_portal_link` | destroy (irreversible) | Mint a temporary link into a contact's customer portal, where they can see their own invoices, estimates and subscriptions. The url authenticates on its own — anyone holding it reaches that contact's documents without logging in — so hand it only to that contact. It expires after 1 hour. |
| `create_customer_portal_invoices_link` | destroy (irreversible) | Mint a temporary link that opens the invoices page of a contact's customer portal. The url grants access to that contact's invoices to whoever holds it, and expires after 1 hour. |
| `create_customer_portal_subscription_link` | destroy (irreversible) | Mint a temporary link that opens one subscription in a contact's customer portal. The subscription must belong to that contact and have a subscription template, otherwise Moneybird answers 404. The url grants access to that subscription to whoever holds it, and expires after 1 hour. |
| `list_verifications` | read | List what the administration has verified about itself: its confirmed sender email addresses and bank account numbers, plus its chamber of commerce and tax number. Keys are absent while a verification is still pending, which makes this the way to check whether sending or direct debit is ready to use. |
